intro: Learn to express what you know, think or say using a subordinate prayer with что.

устала.es: se cansó / estaba cansada (femenino; según el contexto)
устала.en: was tired / tired (feminine; depending on context)

bloques.titulo: To say what you know or think
texto: **Что** can link verbs such as **знать** (know), **думать** (think) and **сказать** (say) with the following information: **Я знаю, что она работает** (I know you work) and **Я думаю, что он придёт** (I think you will come). In these cases, **что** equals «that».

In these phrases, the coma is placed before **что**, which introduces the subordinate information. Then a conjugated verb appears; the subject can be omitted if it is already understood: **Она сказала, что устала** (she said she was tired; it is understood that she was tired). In **Что ты читаешь?** (What do you read?), **что** asks for one thing and means «what».

bloques.titulo: Verbs to know, think and say

opciones.texto: She said she wanted to get tired.
opciones.explicacion: The phrase says she was already tired.
The coma is placed before the subordinate introduced by **что**.
The **я** subject and the **знаю** verb are not separated with a coma.
In this pattern, the coma goes before **что**, not after.
